edit.description: `:548-556` hoists `graph::resolved_edges` and hands the whole declared-field arc set to `graph::acyclic`. Feed acyclicity the import relation instead: the member→member `@import` edges `graph::classify_directives` already returns and `:387` drops on the floor (only `.findings` is read today), plus the lifted layout-prose `import` edges already folded into `mention_edges` at `:197` (`drift::import_edges_from_doc`). `resolved_edges` stays hoisted — `check`, `degree`, and `mention_reachable` keep reading it.

`acyclic` (:241-270): its input becomes the import relation, not `&[ResolvedEdge]` of declared fields. The doc's rationale ("a circular import that loads nothing") is false as written — Claude Code recurses imports to a four-hop cap (cite in notes), so the true positive is the silently truncated tail; `cycle_diagnostic`'s message follows. The in-module cases at :2320-2420 (`a_self_loop_fires_an_acyclic_error`, `a_multi_node_cycle_fires_an_acyclic_error`, `an_inadmissible_edge_is_skipped_by_acyclic`) rebuild over import-relation arcs.

`a_cyclic_reference_graph_fails_the_run` (:305) pins a `routes_to` rule↔skill *field* cycle as a failure — invert it: the field cycle passes, the run is clean. `an_acyclic_reference_graph_passes` (:278) stands. Add the relation the spec does name: two members whose `@import` directives point at each other fire one `graph.acyclic` error.

`gate_resolved_edge_walk_is_hoisted_per_gate_invocation` (:410-460) calls `graph::acyclic(resolved_edges)` as one of the shared consumers of the hoisted walk. Re-point it: acyclic leaves that consumer set, and the once-per-invocation claim is re-pinned over `check`/`degree`/`mention_reachable`.

The `@import` classing's integration home. Its edges stop being dropped at the gate, so the classing's verdict split is asserted here: an unbacked pointer still warns, a member↔member ring now reaches `graph.acyclic`.

summary: `graph::acyclic` ranges over every declared field edge; contract.md scopes acyclicity to the import relation — narrow its input, and let a field-edge cycle pass.

tests.asserts: a `routes_to` rule↔skill field cycle passes `check` clean; a member↔member `@import` ring fires exactly one `graph.acyclic` error naming the chain
the resolved-edge walk is still computed exactly once per `gate()` invocation with acyclic off its consumer list

acceptance: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green. Oracle (the inbox repro): a corpus of two custom kinds whose edge fields point at each other — members `one` ↔ `two` — gives `temper check .` exit 0 with no `graph.*` finding, where it exits 1 today; a `CLAUDE.md` → rule → `CLAUDE.md` `@import` ring fires one `graph.acyclic` error.

edit.description: `KindFacts` becomes generic over the kind's typed surface (new `KindFacts<T extends object = Record<string, unknown>>`) so a new optional leaf-set witness binds to `keyof T`, and `kind<T>` (:476) carries it to the row. 0053 rejects a free author-written leaf schema and rules the corpus supplies the key set *through its typed constructor*, so the witness is compiler-bound, never a loose list: an exhaustive record (`{ [K in keyof T]-?: true }`, where omitting a key is a type error) is the shape that makes a partial set impossible; `readonly (keyof T & string)[]` is the weaker one that admits a subset. `relocate` (:546) rides the base's witness unchanged — a relocation appends edge fields over the kind's own surface, never an embedded leaf — so `relocationInvariants` needs no new erasure.

`kindFactRow` (:345) lowers the witness into the row's `leaves` column, absent when the kind declares none. `kindFactKindsInPlay` (:504) admits an embedded kind only when it declares `guidance`/`cite` — widen it to a declared leaf set, or the column never reaches the lock for the very kinds it exists to teach. The module's erased `KindFacts` signatures (:215, :285, :323, :345, :370, :382, :400, :431, :469-472, :492, :504, :556) ride the generic's default, so no call site re-spells a type argument.
`:69` re-exports the `KindFacts` type — it follows the generic.

The emitted-rows home (the `guidance` row precedent at :482): a kind declaring the witness emits its leaf set on the row in declaration order; a kind declaring none emits no `leaves` key, so `:201`'s exhaustive `deepEqual` over the built-in rows stands unchanged; and an embedded kind whose only declaration is a leaf set now takes a row where it takes none today.
